newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert sees Blair set for role in Europe.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert sees Blair set for role in Europe.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Saturday Britain's new prime minister Tony Blair was a pragmatic man who should be able to play an important role in Europe.
Blair's Labour party swept to a resounding victory in Britain's general election on Thursday, ending 18 years of rule by John Major's Conservatives, who had been deeply split over policy on Europe.

"I think Tony Blair is a man in the good British tradition of pragmatism, so he has integrated into his team people with different sensitivities but a team which it seems...will allow him to play an important role at the heart of the European Union," Van Miert told Belgian RTBF radio.
To play this role "they must not be negative like the Conservatives have been for too long," he added.

"You have to be positive, so have to know also how to make concessions, be among the leading runners. There is...a hope, on the way, that Tony Blair will become one of the important leaders of Europe," he said.
However, he added, "one mustn't get carried away, one mustn't expect miracles".

Van Miert, a Belgian, recalled the late Socialist French President Francois Mitterrand who led his country for 14 years and was praised at his funeral last year as a tireless promoter of European unity.
"Let's not forget that at the beginning Mitterand wasn't especially pro-European either. It's only along the way, in the light of experience that...it turned out that way."
New British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Friday one of his priorities was to improve relations with the EU.

These plummeted last year after the 15-nation bloc slapped an export ban on British beef exports amid fears that mad cow disease could spread to humans. Major briefly suspended all cooperation with the EU in protest. REUTER
